messages.subject: 2 part model
parts:
I have small data set (n=100) with a large spike of unaffected mice
and then a normal distribution of affected ones. The 2 part model
seems the most appropriate model for this data. When I map the data
with this model I get several suggestive qtl after permutation testing
(1000x). This model really tests 4 models simultaneously. In several
instances the overall model is suggestive but the lod.p model is
significant.

Is it appropriate to report the individual results of the lod.p.mu,
lod.p, lod.mu? Is it possible to graph each of the output of this
model by chromosome or genome wide? If so is it possible to add the
individual thresholds (from permutation testing) for each of the
parameters (lod.p.mu, lod.p, lod.mu) to the graph?

Basically, I'd like to show a graph like fig2 of Boyartchuk etal and
I'm having some trouble.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] 2 part model
parts:
Here is some example code:

data(listeria)
listeria <- calc.genoprob(listeria, step=1)
listeria$pheno$T264 <- log2(listeria$pheno$T264)

out <- scanone(listeria, model="2part", upper=TRUE)
operm <- scanone(listeria, model="2part", upper=TRUE, n.perm=100)
thr <- summary(operm, 0.05)

plot(out, lod=1:3, chr=c(1,5,13,15))
abline(h=thr, col=c("black","blue","red"), lty=2)

text(0, thr[1]+0.1, expression(LOD(p,mu)), adj=c(0,0.5))
text(0, thr[2]-0.1, expression(LOD(p)), adj=c(0,0.5), col="blue")
text(0, thr[3]+0.1, expression(LOD(mu)), adj=c(0,0.5), col="red")

karl
